card.title: Theoretical Yield, Experimental Yield and Percentage Yield

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **theoretical yield** (maximum from the limiting reactant), **actual yield** (mass really isolated) and **percentage yield** (actual ÷ theoretical × 100) form chemistry's efficiency triangle: 40 g from a 50 g theoretical yield is 80% (NEB 2024). Actual yield falls short through side reactions, incomplete (equilibrium-limited) conversion, mechanical losses and impure reactants.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - % yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100 - actual = (% ÷ 100) × theoretical - atom economy = (mass of desired product ÷ total mass of products) × 100

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Yield vs atom economy:** yield = actual/theoretical (experiment); atom economy = desired/total product mass (equation design).  ·  **Theoretical vs actual:** theoretical is calculated (paper maximum); actual is weighed (laboratory reality) — always actual ≤ theoretical.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***50 g theoretical, 40 g actual*** — 80% yield (NEB 2024): the standard two-mark numerical.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: theoretical yield, experimental yield, % yield (within Stoichiometry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Theory vs Reality Stoichiometry predicts the **theoretical yield** — the maximum product from complete conversion of the limiting reactant. Real experiments deliver less: the **actual yield**. Their ratio, as a percentage, is the **percentage yield** — chemistry's honest scoreboard.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The three quantities | Quantity | Meaning | How obtained | |---|---|---| | **Theoretical yield** | Maximum product if the limiting reactant converts completely | Stoichiometric calculation | | **Actual yield** | Mass actually isolated in the lab/experiment | Weighed experimentally | | **Percentage yield** | (Actual ÷ theoretical) × 100 | The efficiency measure | $$\%\text{ yield} =…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Actual on top, theoretical below, ×100 — and the answer can never exceed 100%."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (2m): In an experiment, the theoretical yield is 50 g but only 40 g of product is obtained. Calculate the percentage yield.** — % yield = (actual/theoretical) × 100 = (40/50) × 100 = **80%**.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: If asked "why is the actual yield lower?", list side reactions + incomplete conversion + handling losses — three reasons, three marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Theoretical yield comes from the limiting reactant** — never from the excess.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: % yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100. NEB 2024: 40/50 × 100 = 80%. Reasons for loss: side reactions, incomplete reaction, mechanical losses, impurities.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Industrial processes run 90–99% yield; multi-step syntheses multiply losses — ten 90% steps give only ~35% overall.
